各位陛下、列位嘉宾，请再赐片刻静听：今夕之戏，既为娱人，亦为示警。愿诸位以沉思之目观之。吾言既毕，鼓一响即为开场信号，请诸位演员上前表演。
击鼓一响，作为开场信号——诸位演员起，请开始表演。
鼓已响，开场！我们现在开始表演。
First Player: The drum is confirmed — curtain. The performance is now underway; proceed with the play.

Hear now Aeneas' tale to Dido: “Pyrrhus, like the rugged Hyrcanian beast, rushed in with flaming eyes and unsheathed steel. He leapt upon poor Priam — the aged king, fallen at his hearth, struck down before the altar; his blood bespattered the sacred stones and Troy cried out. Hecuba ran barefoot, rending her hair and beating at the doors, while sons and fathers lay heaped about their lord. Thus perished Priam, and Troy reeled beneath the thunder of that slaughter.”

My lords and ladies, your Majesty: though our hearts are heavy with grief for Polonius, let not sorrow unmake the order of this court. Tonight’s little play is offered both as solace and as a mirror to the mind; if it can grant the king and his council a moment’s respite and thought, our task is done. Pray be seated with calm attention — when the drum sounds, the players shall begin. May this short piece both entertain and provoke sober reflection.

message.content: Marcellus: I will wake Horatio at once and bring him to the west side of the battlements by the north tower. We will not approach the figure alone. I will send a runner to the armory for the armorer and storeskeeper and order them to report back with (1) how many men are ready to muster, (2) the counts and condition of weapons and armor, and (3) the amount and condition of powder and shot. I will muster any ready men at the north gate and keep the battlements secured until you or Fortinbras return.

Barnardo, Marcellus — well noted. Hold your watch; do not approach or challenge the figure alone. Barnardo, thank you for sending the runner; muster any ready men at the north gate and keep the battlements secured. Rosencrantz — go fetch Horatio at once and bring him to the north tower to join the watch. When the armorer and storeskeeper arrive, send me immediately their report: (1) how many men are ready to muster at once, (2) counts and condition of weapons and armor, and (3) amount and condition of powder and shot. If the figure moves or any threat appears, raise the alarm and send a runner to me at once.
